description: Things existing in the world before anybody owns them, and staying the same things afterwards (US-3 and US-4 of `124-items-equipment-economy`). Each case carries an authored `WorldIR.items` slice, the world’s loot tables, the catalogue and the seed, and pins what a host materializes: every placement resolved in canonical id order, the `ItemPlace` each row’s contents land in, and what every container turned out to hold. The identity claim is the point and it is two-sided — a placement id is the SCENE NODE’s `entityId` and therefore `editor/reimport/diff.ts`’s match key, while the item atom is what core resolves it back to — so the hand-moved case pins the same chest at a different position holding the same hoard down to the coin. Loot has two paths and one discipline: an authored `systems.lootTables` row rolled per entry, or the catalogue drawn against `item_loot_weight/2` through the same function that stocks a merchant’s shelf, each keyed per `(seed, placement id, cycle, item)` so catalogue order, generation order and how many containers were filled first cannot move a single chest. Regenerate with `npm run items-corpus`.

cases.name: a-barrow-the-world-placed
cases.note: Everything US-3 claims, in one export: a sword lying where nobody owns it, a locked chest stocked from an authored table, and a letter that only ever sits inside that chest. Each row resolves to a place — `item_at/3` for the sword, the chest’s own container for the letter — and the chest’s contents are drawn deterministically from `(seed, placement id, cycle)`.

cases.name: a-creator-moved-the-chest-and-it-is-the-same-chest
cases.note: The re-import claim as data. The identical world with the chest three metres over and turned around: the id is unchanged, so `editor/reimport/diff.ts` matches it, the ledger keys the same container place, and the hoard inside is the same hoard down to the coin. A port that derived a container’s identity from its transform loses a creator’s afternoon here.

cases.name: a-chest-that-names-no-table-draws-from-the-world’s-own-rarity
cases.note: The second loot path: no authored table, so the catalogue is drawn against `item_loot_weight/2` through the SAME function that stocks a merchant’s shelf. A loaf turns up more often than a cuirass because the world said so, not because a loot system has its own opinion.

cases.name: two-chests-in-one-world-hold-different-things
cases.note: The stream’s subject is the placement id, so identical containers in one world are not identical hoards — and neither of them moves when the other is generated first, because no stream is advanced per candidate.

cases.name: the-same-chest-on-the-next-cycle
cases.note: A respawn is the same chest with the cycle advanced, which is what keeps a reload from rerolling a hoard the player already emptied: the fill is a function of the cycle, and the cycle is a save field.

cases.name: a-world-that-authored-its-own-loot-numbers
cases.note: Neither draw count nor depth is core’s: a world that wants a dragon’s pile authors one, and the per-container `draws` overrides even that. Nothing here is a compiled constant.

cases.name: a-world-that-placed-nothing
cases.note: The empty case, which is the shape of every world that did not author a placement: no rows, no containers, no draws — and the world’s tuning still resolved, so a host asking for it gets numbers rather than an absence.
